title: Machine learning ranks drugs from cholangiocarcinoma phosphoproteomes
summary: Phosphoproteomes of 13 primary cholangiocarcinoma tumours with matched tissue and 7 cell lines (over 13,000 phosphorylation sites) were analysed with DRUML (Drug Ranking Using Machine Learning), which ranked HDAC inhibitors (belinostat, CAY10603) and PI3K inhibitors highly. The rankings were confirmed in cholangiocarcinoma cell-line models. Small cohort, proof of concept, cell lines only, and effect sizes were not read.
ai_technology: DRUML (Drug Ranking Using Machine Learning) on phosphoproteomic profiles
organization: King's College London; Foundation for Liver Research; King's College Hospital

evidence.tested: Computational drug rankings tested in cholangiocarcinoma cell lines.
evidence.unknown: Effect sizes; activity in patients; full text not reviewed.
